title: Latency Degradation Policy and Recovery Cookbook
author: Aisha Tan
body:
Summary:

This cookbook documents Redwood Inference's standard policy and prescriptive remediation workflows for production latency degradation incidents. It is intended for SREs on-call, model-serving engineers, and platform owners. The focus is on fast detection, automated containment, safe capacity moves, and clear manual recovery actions that preserve SLOs and customer experience.

Scope:
- Applies to all model-serving endpoints exposed by the Redwood API and Dedicated pools.
- Covers tiered latency SLOs (interactive, high-throughput, background) and includes automated mitigations, manual runbook steps, rollback patterns, communication templates, and post-incident actions.

Motivation:
- Latency degradations are the most common customer-facing reliability issue for inference workloads. They can be caused by traffic spikes, model regressions, kernel hotpaths, KV cache eviction storms, or hardware/network flakiness. This cookbook standardizes a fast, low-risk response pattern.

Key SLOs and Error-Budget Policy (examples):
- Interactive (default public API): p99 < 1.2s, p95 < 350ms.
- High-throughput (batch/embeddings): p90 < 1.0s, median < 300ms.
- Background (async queuing): median < 2.0s, p95 < 3.5s.

Error budget burn / policy thresholds (global per-service rolling 7d):
- Green: burn < 10% — monitor only.
- Advisory: 10% <= burn < 40% — paging to owner, review recent deploys.
- Mitigation: 40% <= burn < 70% — automated soft mitigation (circuit-breaker throttles, reduce batch sizes).
- Emergency: burn >= 70% — aggressive actions (evict heavy tenants, fall back to cheaper model variants, apply global rate limit).

Service Impact Matrix (quick reference):
- Severity P2 (degraded latency but healthy error rates): follow Mitigation path.
- Severity P1 (latency + error increase impacting SLAs): follow Emergency path and invoke Incident War Room.

Alerting & Telemetry Requirements:
- Primary latency alert: rolling 5m p95 > threshold for 3 consecutive 1m windows.
- Secondary burn alert: 7d error-budget burn rate crossing 40% (advisory) and 70% (emergency).
- Synthetic canary failures: any canary latency regression > 2x baseline triggers advisory.
- Required telemetry: per-tenant tokenized latency histograms, backend queue depth, GPU utilization (per-pool), KV-cache-miss-rate, model-variant selector logs, routing fallback counts.

Dashboards (what to look at):
- Global SLO overview (p50/p90/p95/p99) with error-budget curve.
- Pool-level telemetry: GPU util, memory pressure, kernel preemption events, running processes per-GPU.
- Traffic composition: top 5 tenants by RPS, percent of streaming vs blocking requests.
- Model health: recent commits, quantization profile in use, kernel variant in production.

Automated mitigation primitives (ordered by least-to-most impact):
1) Per-route soft throttles: reduce concurrency from 32 -> 8 for suspect route.
2) Prefer lower-latency model variant (e.g., quantized AUTOQ-8) for new requests.
3) Serve from warmed KV cache snapshots for active prefixes.
4) Reduce default max_tokens or tokenization chunking for suspects.
5) Autoscale: spin up warm nodes (hot-pool burst) based on GPU pool elasticity policy.
6) Tenant-level fairshare evictions (last-resort): pre-approved eviction list and billing-triggered preemption.

Runbook: detection and automated response (step-by-step)
1) Detection (automated):
   - Pager fires when p95 > threshold for 3 x 1m windows OR 7d burn >= 40%.
   - Runbook heartbeat: automated triage job fetches latest 5m stacks, identifies top N routes/tenants by latency.
2) Pre-emptive automated steps (executed by orchestration):
   - Validate canary health; if canary healthy, skip to step 4.
   - If canary degraded, apply model-variant fallback (AUTOQ -> FP16 fallback disabled to preserve accuracy) and re-evaluate.
   - Execute per-route soft throttle for top-3 offending routes.
3) SRE On-call initial triage (human):
   - Use the SRE incident template to open an incident with severity, affected routes, and initial hypothesis.
   - Check recent deploys (last 60m) and kernel updates; flag any deploy IDs.
4) Capacity-inspired mitigations (if automation insufficient):
   - Command to scale warm nodes: redwoodctl capacity extend --pool <pool-id> --count <n> --reason "latency mitigation"
   - Recommended warm scale increment: +20% of current healthy nodes (cap to burst policy).
   - If GPU memory pressure > 85% across nodes, reduce batch_size for suspect routes: redwoodctl model-config set --model <id> --batch-size <reduced>
5) Traffic shaping and routing changes:
   - Enable fallback routing to dedicated pools: redwoodctl routing update --route <route-id> --target-pool <pool-id-dedicated> --weight 20
   - For immediate relief, apply global streaming-to-nonstreaming degrade: toggle streaming buffer to 0.5s.
6) Escalate if mitigation not restoring SLOs in 10 minutes: follow Emergency path.

Emergency path (if error budget burn >= 70% or p99 > 3x threshold):
- Open War Room; notify on-call lead, product owner, and customer success for affected tenants.
- Execute aggressive actions:
  1) Circuit-break top 5 offending tenants by token usage for 60s and notify teams.
  2) Disable non-essential features (batch reranking, expensive tool-calls) using feature gates.
  3) Apply global rate limit: redwoodctl quota enforce --scope global --rps <value> --reason "emergency-throttle"
  4) Evict non-enterprise preemptible tenants from dedicated pools (pre-approved list executed by automation).

Manual rollback and verification:
- If a recent deploy is suspected, rollback the deploy using the standard deployment rollback playbook:
  1) Identify deploy id from tracer: tracer query 'deploy.id' --last 120m
  2) Rollback: redwoodctl deploy rollback --service <service> --to <previous-release> --wait 120
  3) Verify p95/p99 over next 10 minutes stabilized, then begin gradual traffic reintroduction (10% every 5m).

Post-incident learning and follow-up (within 72h):
1) Postmortem owner: SRE on-call. Draft includes timeline, root cause hypothesis, evidence, mitigations applied, and follow-up action items with owners.
2) Standard required follow-ups:
   - Create a telemetry gap ticket if any required metric was missing.
   - Add a synthetic canary variation that reproduces the condition.
   - If mitigation required scaling policy change, create a capacity-change RFC and schedule a canary.
3) Error-budget policy update: if mitigation occurred more than twice for same root cause in 30d, escalate to SRE leadership for SLO adjustment or architectural remediation.

Roles and responsibilities (owners):
- First responder (SRE on-call): execute runbook, timeline, initial comms.
- Platform runtime lead: approve large-scale capacity moves and pool reconfigurations.
- Model owner: validate model-variant fallbacks and approve accuracy trade-offs.
- Customer Success: coordinate messages for enterprise tenants if impacted.

Comms templates (short):
- Slack incident header: [INCIDENT] Latency degradation — Service: <service> — Severity: <P1|P2> — On-call: <name>
- Customer-facing blurb (initial): "We are investigating increased latency affecting some requests. We have applied mitigations and will follow up with a timeline and impact summary."

Appendix A — Example alert rules (Prometheus style, simplified):
- Alert: HighP95Latency
  Expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) > <route_threshold>
  For: 3m
  Labels: severity=page, team=serving-runtime

- Alert: ErrorBudgetBurn40
  Expr: (error_budget_consumed_7d / error_budget_total_7d) > 0.40
  For: 15m
  Labels: severity=page, team=sre

Appendix B — Useful redwoodctl snippets:
- Scale warm nodes: redwoodctl capacity extend --pool pool-ml-1 --count 4 --reason "latency recovery"
- Throttle route: redwoodctl routing throttle --route route-embed-123 --concurrency 8 --dur 600
- Swap model variant: redwoodctl model set-variant --service inference-api --route /chat --variant autoq-8 --reason "latency fallback"

Appendix C — Quick decision matrix (summary):
- p95 over threshold for < 7m + low GPU util (<60%): investigate kernel/queue regressions, apply software mitigations.
- p95 over threshold + GPU util > 85%: scale warm nodes or shed low-priority tenants.
- p99 large spike + error rate rising: escalate to Emergency path.

References and related pages:
- See SRE deployment rollback playbook and capacity-onboarding-checklist for pre-approval lists.
- Attach incident evidence and runbook execution transcript to the postmortem.
